findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects stored in this bucket are not encrypted at rest by default, risking exposure of sensitive report data if underlying storage is compromised.

No 'acl' attribute or public access block is set, leaving the bucket's access control ambiguous and potentially defaulting to a less restrictive ACL; combined with no encryption this increases risk of data exposure.
The bucket storing ledger export data does not configure server_side_encryption_configuration, so sensitive financial data is stored unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, leaving model artifacts unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, leaving operational runbook data (which may contain sensitive infrastructure details) unencrypted at rest.

The bucket uses the 'log-delivery-write' canned ACL which grants the S3 log delivery group WRITE and READ_ACP permissions; while intended for log delivery, this is a broad grant that should be paired with bucket policy restrictions to avoid unintended write access.

force_destroy = true allows the bucket and all its contents to be deleted without recovery, which combined with no versioning or replication increases risk of irreversible data loss if misused via automation or compromised credentials.

The object is uploaded without specifying server-side encryption (kms_key_id or server_side_encryption), so it inherits the bucket's lack of default encryption, leaving the vendor roster file unencrypted at rest.
